integrity: The exact trace variance formula and pairwise allocation framework are credited to the motivating literature. The asserted contribution is the uniform sharp decay threshold and the closed allocation profiles. All proofs and computational evidence are specified, and no independent validation is asserted.
scientific_limitations: Exact top-eigenpair deflation and exact Gaussian logarithmic quadratic forms are assumed; their computational expense is represented only by a stipulated integer cost.
The universal threshold is for nonnegative adjacent-ratio log spectra and a finite, exactly budgeted ideal estimator family, not practical randomized Nystrom compression or Lanczos quadrature.
Infinite geometric and polynomial laws concern summable diagonal Gaussian series rather than infinite-dimensional standard Gaussian vectors.
The work does not establish high-probability or general trace-estimator optimality.
title: Sharp spectral-decay threshold for one-probe log-determinant estimation
